articles.title: African fintech fund closes at $26m for early-stage startups
articles.snippet: African fintech fund closes at $26m for early-stage startups Geeky Nigeria
articles.text:
Technology
African fintech fund closes at $26m for early-stage startups
Omotolani Ajileye 20 November 2026, 10:45 WAT 5 min read Blockchain, cryptocurrency and network. Graphic: Maiconfz / Pixabay
Africa Fund I, the first fund raised by women-led investor First Circle Capital, has reached a final close of $26 million. The money is earmarked for young African fintech businesses, regardless of which country on the continent they are based in. The firm says such capital is necessary because founders across Africa continue to find it hard to secure pre-seed funding . Beyond fintechs in their early days , First Circle Capital also has a public profile as a women-led investor .
Africa Fund I focus on startups at the very first stages of fundraising, meaning rounds before and at the initial seed stage, that develop financial products and services or the underlying infrastructure that supports them. It is particularly keen on firms applying AI, automation and data analysis to help the financial sector operate more efficiently.
Backers of the fund include the International Finance Corporation (IFC), Bpifrance, Egypt's Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises Development Agency (MSMEDA), Axian, the Dutch Good Growth Fund, Stellar Foundation and FSD Africa.
Why African fintech still draws investors
Financial technology still attracts a large share of startup funding in Africa, although venture capital investors are growing more cautious and spreading their money across fewer deals. African startups raised a combined $3.42 billion in 2025, and fintech accounted for $1.37 billion of that, or 40% of the total.
Even after ten years of rapid growth in online payments and credit, First Circle Capital is convinced that Africa's next wave of fintech firms will grow out of problems that are still unsolved, and it is backing that belief with its money.
In a statement setting out what Africa Fund I is for, Selma Ribica, who is managing partner and co-founder of First Circle Capital, said the vehicle rests on a simple belief: tomorrow's leading fintech companies in Africa will be the ones tackling the deep-seated barriers that keep so many people across the continent from accessing banking and other financial products. She said the firm wants to spot those companies at the very start of their journey and to partner closely with the founders behind them while they grow.
The team and the FinTech 2.0 strategy
First Circle Capital was set up in 2021 by Ribica, who previously held an executive post at M-Pesa and now invests in fintech, together with Agnes Aistleitner and Robert Smith. Offices in Kampala, Nairobi, Casablanca, and Cape Town serve a continent-wide mandate that takes in Nigeria, Kenya, South Africa, Egypt, Morocco, Uganda, Ghana, and Francophone Africa.
The firm calls its strategy FinTech 2.0. Its focus areas cover insurance technology, new credit and lending structures, interoperability and the underlying plumbing of finance, climate-oriented fintech, SaaS products for financial services, and reg tech. It also favours AI-native startups in African fintech , meaning companies that embed artificial intelligence in their operations and are data-driven from the outset.

SRS Real Estate Partners Announces the $17 Million Acquisition of a Single-Tenant Albertsons Property in Ardmore, Oklahoma
November 20, 2026
SRS Real Estate Partners announced today it has completed the $17 million acquisition of an Albertsons-occupied property located at 1855 12th Ave NW in Ardmore, OK. Built in 2025, the 50,751-square-foot property is situated on 4.73 acres and has a long-term, absolute triple net, corporate-guaranteed lease in place.
SRS Capital Markets Vice President Joe Chichester and Senior Vice President John Redfield represented the buyer, a Newport Beach-based private family office in the acquisition as part of a 1031 exchange. The seller was an investment firm from Texas. The closing cap rate was 5.35%.
“We worked closely with the buyer to help navigate the sale of their relinquished property before successfully representing them in the acquisition of this Albertsons through a 1031 exchange,” said Chichester. “With 19 years remaining on the lease, a corporate guaranty, and minimal landlord responsibilities, the property provides our client with a stable, long-term income stream that aligns with their investment objectives.”
The property is part of a larger retail center that includes Academy Sports, PetSmart, Burlington, and Panda Express, among other tenants, creating favorable cross over traffic.
This year, SRS Capital Markets has completed more than $2.5 billion in deal volume comprised of more than 500 transactions across the nation. SRS currently has in excess of 900 properties actively on the market with a market value surpassing $4.3 billion.
About SRS Real Estate Partners
Founded in 1986, SRS Real Estate Partners is celebrating 40 years of going the extra mile for its clients. A leader in consumer-driven real estate, SRS provides commercial real estate solutions across retail, industrial, and capital markets. Headquartered in Dallas with 30 offices nationwide, the firm measures its success by the achievement of its clients’ objectives, satisfaction, and trust. For more information, please visit srsre.com .

articles.title: On-Device Hyper-Personalized AI Startup SAKAK Secures Strategic Investment From DRB Dongil
articles.snippet: On-Device Hyper-Personalized AI Startup SAKAK Secures Strategic Investment From DRB Dongil Wowtale
articles.text:
SAKAK , an AI company specializing in hyper-personalized artificial intelligence, has raised a strategic investment of about 200 million won from DRB Dongil , according to a disclosure filed on Nov. 19.
SAKAK resolved to carry out a third-party allocation of new shares to DRB Dongil, issuing the shares to a party other than its existing shareholders. The new shares are 13,378 redeemable convertible preferred shares (RCPS), with a par value of 100 won and an issue price of 14,950 won per share. The total issuance comes to about 200 million won (200,001,100 won).
Founded in 2022, SAKAK is a deep-tech AI startup that holds on-device hyper-personalized AI solution technology. Its stated aim is to shed light on society’s blind spots with data and AI. It developed HyPAA (Hyper-Personalized AI Agent) in-house, an agent designed to keep data from being exposed or leaked outside, even in environments that handle sensitive information. Customers can adopt only the functions they need or receive customized AI consulting. SAKAK builds and supplies AI tailored to each client in four stages: AI consulting, data collection, custom AI development and service deployment.
Its flagship solution, CANDiY, is a product line that helps make healthcare data usable for AI:
Candiy API integrates AI-optimized healthcare data, including medical records, wearable device data and insurance information, and delivers it through an API.
Candiy Pocket manages personal information and sensitive data using double encryption.
Candiy OCR converts complex medical and financial documents into digital form.
SAKAK also offers a domain-specific generative AI assistant that applies retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to answer questions based on specialized knowledge and can run on a home GPU. It supports both cloud and on-premises installation and has been applied to insurance coverage analysis and treatment suggestions, medical document summarization and automation of insurance loss adjustment work.
In November 2025, SAKAK signed a business agreement with Dongguk University Ilsan Hospital to develop an AI health coordinator solution. In June 2025, it was selected as one of five Korean representative startups in the Qualcomm AI Innovation Program 2025. Its other recognitions include a place among the global top 20 at the MWC 2025 4YFN Awards, selection as a MyData operator in the 2022 MyData Operator Award and the top prize at the 2023 Youth Startup Academy Dream Show.

PawSwing
PawSwing makes a cat house that grooms your cat while your cat does nothing out of the ordinary.
A bionic brush arch at the entrance combs out loose fur every time your cat walks in or out, and keeps it
in the house instead of on your furniture.
The PawSwing app
The app connects to your PawSwing house over Bluetooth. It runs a training plan that lowers the brush a
little each day so your cat gets used to it, lets you set the brush yourself at any time, and keeps the
record: which days your cat used the house and for how long, the battery, firmware updates, and a profile
for each cat. Sign in with your email address or with Google.
